Threat.value: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building

Memory.value: I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it
When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel isolated and set apart from others
There is something about me that made the event happen
I can't stop bad things from happening to me

vignette: Rafael Hernandez had always been drawn to the creative precision of architecture. As a successful architect in his late forties, he took pride in designing spaces that felt both functional and beautiful. But it was on one fateful evening, while working late at his office, that Rafael's life took an abrupt turn. He witnessed a violent altercation between two strangers outside his building, an event that would forever sear itself into his memory. As the days passed, Rafael found himself increasingly on edge. The sound of raised voices or the scent of cigarette smoke – reminiscent of that night – could send him spiraling back to the traumatic scene. He'd feel a familiar wave of nausea wash over him, and before he knew it, he was reliving the event as if it were happening all over again. His memories of that night remained stubbornly disjointed, refusing to cohere into a linear narrative. When attempting to recount the events to his wife or colleagues, Rafael would struggle to find the words, as if the language itself had been torn from him. As time went on, these triggers began to exert an insidious influence over Rafael's daily life. Upon entering any room or building, he'd instinctively scan for exits, a habit that left him feeling jumpy and easily startled. He couldn't shake the sense of being exposed unless his back was against a wall where he could see the entire space unfold before him. This hyper-vigilance had become second nature to Rafael; it was as if his mind had become wired to constantly scan for threats. These intrusive thoughts also led Rafael down a dark path of self-blame and negative appraisals. He'd convinced himself that there must be something fundamentally flawed within him, some intrinsic fault that made him a magnet for such horrors. This gnawing sense of helplessness had isolated him from those around him – friends, family, even his wife. They couldn't possibly understand what he was going through; Rafael felt like an outsider looking in on his own life. As the weeks turned into months, Rafael's avoidance behaviors began to take a toll on his relationships and work. His wife, Maria, grew increasingly concerned about his withdrawal from social events and family gatherings. At the office, Rafael found himself struggling to concentrate, his designs marred by mistakes and missteps. It was as if the traumatic event had awakened a persistent threat response within him – always lurking just beneath the surface, waiting to pounce. One day, while working on a new project, Rafael's anxiety spiked when he caught a whiff of cigarette smoke wafting from outside his office window. The scent instantly transported him back to that fateful night, and with it came the familiar wave of nausea and disorientation. His mind racing, Rafael quickly excused himself, citing a sudden case of food poisoning as an excuse for his abrupt departure. In truth, Rafael knew he couldn't outrun these triggers forever. He was exhausted from living in this constant state of high alert, trapped within a self-reinforcing cycle of threat and fear. As the days went by, Rafael began to realize that he needed help – not just to manage his symptoms but to break free from the crushing weight of his own negative appraisals. As he sat in his dimly lit office, staring blankly at the computer screen, Rafael finally made the decision to seek professional help. He knew it wouldn't be easy, but he couldn't shake the feeling that there had to be more to life than this suffocating fog of anxiety and fear. For the first time in months, a glimmer of hope flickered within him – perhaps with guidance, Rafael could learn to tame his inner demons and find a way back to the person he once was.
